readback.name: Poincare.MetricAdaptedGlobalParametrix.exists_metric_adapted_global_parametrix
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E3 be EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), the real three-dimensional Euclidean vector space. For arbitrary universe u, let M : Type u be a compact Hausdorff topological space with an E3 charted-space structure and a C-infinity IsManifold structure for the identity model with corners over R. Let g0 be any actual ClosedSmoothRiemannianMetric 3 M, a smooth positive-definite Riemannian metric, and let alpha be real with 0 < alpha < 1. There is no connectedness, curvature, positive-Einstein, recognition, flow, atlas, operator, or norm-bound package supplied as an extra hypothesis. The conclusion first constructs one AtlasData A on M. This includes a finite family of genuine extended charts C_i at selected anchors, subordinate open covering regions whose closures lie in their chart sources and have compact coordinate images, and a smooth partition of unity p_i. Write Q_i = coordSupport A i = C_i image tsupport(p_i). Topological support is the closure of the nonzero set. C-infinity everywhere below is the ENat top injected into WithTop ENat. The conclusion constructs scalar families psi_i and xi_i on all of E3, before the time interval is selected. Each psi_i is globally C-infinity, compactly supported, takes values in [0,1], and equals one on a full ambient Euclidean neighborhood of every point of Q_i. Each xi_i is globally C-infinity, compactly supported, takes values in [0,1], equals one pointwise on every point of tsupport(psi_i), and has its topological support inside the actual target of C_i. The fixed GeodesicTransport cutoff based at the same anchor equals one on a full ambient neighborhood of every point of tsupport(xi_i). The xi-equals-one premise on tsupport(psi_i) is pointwise, while the psi and fixed-background-cutoff conditions are germ conditions using nhds. The theorem also constructs simultaneous families theta_ij : E3 -> R and F_ij : E3 -> E3 before time. For every ordered chart pair, theta_ij is globally C-infinity, compactly supported, and [0,1]-valued. Its support lies in source(C_i.symm.trans C_j), requiring supported coordinates z to be in target(C_i) with C_i.symm(z) in source(C_j). It equals one on a full ambient neighborhood of every point of K_ij = C_i image (tsupport(p_i) intersect (C_j.symm image tsupport(xi_j))). F_ij is globally C-infinity and compactly supported, and agrees on a full ambient neighborhood of every point of tsupport(theta_ij) with the actual i-to-j coordinate transition change A i j = C_j composed with C_i.symm. For each pair there exists L : NNReal making F_ij globally LipschitzWith L. This constant can vary by pair; no single explicit Lipschitz constant or injectivity, inverse, or affine condition is asserted. The support condition on theta is the genuine transition source; the literal type does not additionally require theta-support containment in a background-cutoff-one locus or F-support containment in that transition source. The conclusion next constructs real constants Cpsi,CP,Cglobal,tau and a real transport-bound array CB_ijcd, all before the subsequent universal time quantifier. Cpsi and CP are nonnegative, every CB_ijcd is nonnegative, and 0 < tau <= 1. Cglobal is exactly CP multiplied by the finite sum over all chart indices i,j and component indices c,d : Fin 3 of CB_ijcd; hence its nonnegativity follows from that equality and the stated signs. The geometry and these constants can depend on M,g0,alpha and the selected witnesses, but they are uniform for all 0 < T <= tau. For every such T, the theorem constructs local continuous real-linear maps S_i : Scalar alpha T -> Jet alpha T and R_i : Scalar alpha T -> Scalar alpha T, actual entry transports B_ijcd : SourceGraphs alpha T -> Jet alpha T, and Pglobal : Y_M A alpha T -> X_M A alpha T. Scalar is the original scalar Y space; Jet is the original Graph space with u,ut,du,ddu, zero initial u trace, genuine spatial derivative certificates within the closed time interval, and the within-Icc 0 T time derivative certificate. Each Y field is zero off the cylinder Icc 0 T times E3. Each Y norm is its value supremum plus its within-cylinder alpha-Hoelder seminorm using distance norm(x-y) + sqrt(abs(t-s)); each Graph norm is the sum of its four Y norms. SourceGraphs is the nine-Graph finite Pi space with its existing maximum norm. Y_M and X_M use the original inherited finite Pi/submodule norms of compatible Scalar and Graph entry families, respectively. Their tensor-submodule conditions use scalar or u evaluations for spatial support, component symmetry, and the partition-weighted overlap law. No new norm, completeness hypothesis, or alternative NormedSpace instance is introduced. For each local chart i, S_i has the unconditional spatial u-support property that (S_i f).u(t,z) = 0 outside tsupport(psi_i), for every scalar input f and every ambient point. In contrast, the residual identity and both local estimates are asserted only for inputs f that vanish whenever their spatial coordinate is outside Q_i, at all ambient times. For such supported f and every ambient p, R_i f(p) = chartValue a_i (S_i f)(p) - f(p), with a_i(z) obtained by explicitly invoking the Matrix.inv instance on the entire Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R value inverseChartPullbackGramMatrixField g0 (anchor_i) z. This field is the coordinate Gram matrix of the metric pulled back through the inverse chart; the applied inverse is the full matrix inverse, not entrywise reciprocal and not pointwise inversion of a function. The pinned chartValue is the actual variable-coefficient principal scalar operator G.ut(t,z) minus the double sum of a_i(z)_(m,n) * G.ddu(t,z)(e_m)(e_n). Thus the residual sign is R_i f = L_i(S_i f) - f, equivalently L_i S_i = id + R_i on the supported inputs. Its norm is at most Cpsi * (T^((1-alpha)/2) + T^(1-alpha/2)) * norm(f), and norm(S_i f) <= CP * norm(f), with the powers interpreted as real powers. These are not unrestricted operator-norm bounds for S_i or R_i on the whole Scalar space. Every B_ijcd has operator norm at most the same pre-time CB_ijcd. For every arbitrary nine-Graph family w and every ambient p=(t,z), its u value is the double sum over a,b : Fin 3 of weight A i theta_ij xi_j F_ij a b c d z * (w(a,b)).u(t,F_ij(z)). The pinned weight is theta_ij(z) * (p_i(C_i.symm(z)) * xi_j(F_ij(z)) * (D F_ij at z, applied to e_c)_a * (D F_ij at z, applied to e_d)_b). Only destination partition p_i is inserted. Each such B also has u zero outside Q_i for every w and every real evaluation time. On source(C_i), its u chart value is p_i(x) times the explicitly source-indicated double sum of xi_j(C_j(x)) * jac A i j x a c * jac A i j x b d * (w(a,b)).u(t,C_j(x)); the indicator is @ite R with Classical.propDecidable for x in source(C_j), and its off-source branch is zero. The Jacobian maps i coordinates to j coordinates, with output/source-field indices a,b and input/destination-field indices c,d. No source partition p_j factor is added. Finally, norm(Pglobal) <= Cglobal, and for every forcing f in Y_M and every i,c,d, the complete Graph entry (Pglobal f).val(i,c,d) equals the finite sum over all source charts j of B_ijcd applied to the nine-component family (a,b) |-> S_j(f.val(j,a,b)). This is full Graph equality, fixing u,ut,du,ddu and their existing certificates through the actual assembled expression, rather than an equality of u values alone or bare existence of an unspecified bounded map. The codomain X_M supplies the original tensor-submodule compatibility. The theorem additionally states, for every real t and every x in source(C_i), the exact u chart-value identity with value A xi W i c d x, where W_jab(z) = (S_j(f.val(j,a,b))).u(t,z). That pinned value sums every source contribution with its genuine source-chart indicator, source outer buffer, two actual Jacobians, and destination partition only. All displayed local residual, transport, support, and chart evaluations are on the whole ambient product where stated, with the time zero extensions retaining consistency outside the cylinder. The selected A,buffers,gate maps,local solvers,transport maps and global map are outputs from g0 and alpha, not premises. The result does not construct a bounded global L or global residual R, state a full DeTurck identity including lower-order terms, assert norm of a global R below one, solve nonlinear inversion, establish ordinary joint C3 at initial time zero, or produce physical Ricci flow, favorable Hamilton convergence, smoothability, or the final Poincare theorem.
